settings.eyebrow: HomeSieve by Braivex · Property listings copilot
settings.heading: HomeSieve
settings.lede:
A property listings copilot for commercial property.
HomeSieve reads live listings from five sources into one index, scores each one against your brief, reads the photos, and answers in plain language.
Every answer cites the listing it came from.
settings.metric: Five live listing sources, two of them scrapers we built

settings.label: Ask in plain language
settings.value:
Describe the unit you want the way you would to a colleague: size, budget, area, frontage, use.
The copilot searches the index and streams back the listings that fit as it reads.

settings.label: Hybrid retrieval, reranked
settings.value:
Every listing is embedded and full-text indexed.
A query runs both searches, fuses the results, and a second model reranks the top candidates before anything is written.
A rare word in your brief is not lost to a vector average.

settings.label: Enriched and scored
settings.value:
Size, use class and features are extracted from the listing text where the portal left them out.
Each listing is scored against comparables and against your brief.
The score is shown next to it.

settings.label: Photos, read
settings.value:
A vision model reads the listing photos.
A glazed corner, a mezzanine or a loading door counts even when the agent's description never mentioned it.

settings.label: Watch profiles and alerts
settings.value:
Save a brief as a watch profile and get an alert when a new listing matches.
A map view and a watchlist keep the shortlist where the team can see it.

settings.label: Sources on your budget
settings.value:
Five live sources today, two of them on scrapers we built ourselves after the third-party ones returned blanks.
Scraping runs behind an on/off switch and a budget, so the data bill never surprises you.

settings.heading: A copilot that has read every listing and shows you which.
settings.lede: Built for investors, agents and occupiers who search across portals and would rather ask once.

settings.heading: A property answer without its listing is a rumour.
settings.body:
Language models will happily describe a unit that does not exist.
HomeSieve only answers from listings in its index.
Every claim in the answer links to the listing and the field it came from: the price as listed, the size as stated, the feature as photographed.
If the index has nothing that fits, it says so.
settings.quote: Every answer links the listing it came from. If it cannot, it does not answer.

settings.q: Which markets and sources does it cover?
settings.a:
The five live sources today are UK property portals, two of them on scrapers we built ourselves.
New markets are added per customer.
Each source is a scraper we build or license and run on your budget, so ask about yours.

settings.q: Can it make up a listing?
settings.a:
No.
Answers come only from listings in the index, and every claim links to the listing and the field it came from.
If nothing fits your brief, it tells you so instead of inventing a match.

Sources sync on a schedule you control, with an on/off switch and a monthly budget for scraping.
Each listing shows when it was posted and when it was last seen.

settings.q: Is my team's data separate from other customers'?
settings.a:
Yes.
Every customer has their own workspace with admin and agent roles.
Shortlists, watch profiles and alerts stay inside that workspace.

The copilot is built and indexing live listings.
We onboard early-access customers ourselves.
They tell us which sources and markets they need, and they keep their launch price.

settings.title: Bring a brief. We will bring the listings.
settings.desc:
Tell us the market you search and the kind of unit you want.
We set up your workspace and sources, and you ask the first question.

settings.title: The operator's morning brief.
settings.desc:
BriefSieve reads ads, sales, stock, email and marketplaces overnight and tells you what changed.
A guru explains the numbers and is never allowed to calculate them.

settings.heading: Search every portal once. Get the answer with its source.
